listenings.text: Before any delegation arrives, I check three things. First, the visas. Some visitors have to apply for a visa, and the paperwork can take weeks, so I send the list of requirements on the first day. Second, the budget. Our director has to approve it before I can sign any contract. And third, the venue. I always have a backup plan, because a hotel once cancelled one week before an event. That was a terrible week. I also tell the visitors clearly what is mandatory and what is optional. Registration is mandatory. The city tour and the dinner are optional. They do not have to come, but most people do.

A few years ago, we had a booth at a trade fair in Canada. Everything was ready: the products, the booth, the flights. Then, four days before the fair, someone from the organization called us. We had forgotten a form. Every exhibitor had to send it, because it was about safety. It was mandatory. It was urgent, and we spent two nights doing the paperwork. In the end, they approved it, but it was very close. Now my team has a simple rule. On the first day of any project, we make a list of all the requirements, and we check it every week. It sounds boring, but it works.

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: to follow a rule or a law
that needs attention or action immediately
the forms and documents you need for something official
that you can choose to do or not to do
the possibility that something bad will happen
a second plan, ready in case the first one fails
required by a rule; you cannot choose
something that you must have or do, because a rule says so

paras: When a foreign delegation visits Brazil for a trade mission, the organizers usually start six weeks before. Most of the work is simple: book the hotel, organize the meetings, prepare the program. But experienced organizers know that three risks can ruin the visit, and they check them first.

The first risk is the paperwork. Some visitors have to apply for a visa, and every country has different requirements. The organizers should send a list of documents early, because a delay at the consulate can take weeks. The second risk is the approval of the budget. The director has to approve the costs before the chamber can sign any contract, so this cannot wait until the last week.

The third risk is the venue. A good organizer always has a backup plan: a second hotel, a second meeting room. The visitors do not have to know about the backup plan, but the team must have it ready. Finally, organizers should say clearly what is mandatory and what is optional. Registration is mandatory, but the city tour and the dinner are optional. When the rules are clear, visitors relax, and the visit starts well.
